Seminar Title:

Data Imputation in Healthcare Datasets Using Optimization Methods

Speaker Name:

Convention Room

Contact:

Pabitra Mohan Khilar

Abstract:

Missing data tends to lower the reliability and accuracy of predictive models in data analysis and machine learning because of errors committed during human input, missing diagnostics or contradictory reporting. A method using the Enhanced Firefly Algorithm (EFA) is reported in the first study for class-wise data imputation in healthcare datasets. The predictive model accuracy improved by 16.43%, 18.53% and 22.64% on the healthcare datasets such as Diabetes, Stroke, Heart and Parkinson's Disease datasets, respectively, using this approach, which lowered reconstruction error while preserving class margins. The second work aimed at enhancing imputation precision using an improved DBSCAN algorithm that integrated with Random Forest (RF) and a Multi-Verse Optimizer (MVO). In dermatological and other reference datasets, the hybrid optimization clustering strategy successfully recognized local data patterns with improvements in MAE, MSE, RMSE and R2 by 16.85%, 26.35%, 16.03% and 4.06% respectively. The third work improved the framework by using a fuzzy clustering-based model together with the Marine Predators Algorithm (MPA) to handle overlapping and inconsistent data areas. Compared to existing methods, this method enhanced imputation precision and reduced convergence time using fuzzy memberships and adaptive optimization to handle ambiguity in healthcare data. For high-dimensional, mixed-type healthcare data under MCAR scenarios, the fourth study proposed a Self-Organizing Hybrid Clustering Imputation (SOHCI) framework. Error variance and covariance analysis are employed to dynamically optimize cluster frameworks, which allow the SOHCI model to become scalable with robustness and minimize total imputation error for a set of different healthcare datasets. The findings contribute an integrated, optimization-based framework that enables reliable healthcare analytics, increases data completeness and enhances the efficacy of predictive and decision-support systems.
